summary: Block 12 West -- the 1.6-acre parcel that OCII's August 2026 presentation calls the last remaining development parcel in Mission Bay South (listed as vacant land in the 2015 property management plan) -- is the subject of a preliminary, not-yet-approved MOU between OCII and landowner FOCIL-MB LLC to subdivide the site into a roughly 1.16-acre, ~265-unit 100%-affordable project (up to 90 ft) and a roughly 0.43-acre, ~270-unit market-rate project with inclusionary affordable units (up to 250 ft); the OCII Commission's September 1, 2026 agenda did not include the MOU.

milestones.text: The Successor Agency's Approved Long-Range Property Management Plan for Mission Bay lists Block 12 West (APN 8710-006, 'Northeast corner of Channel Street and Mission Bay Drive') among the Mission Bay South 'Affordable Housing Parcels' the Developer (then Catellus, now FOCIL-MB) is obligated to contribute under the 1998 Owner Participation Agreement -- establishing the parcel as a designated future affordable-housing development site years before the 2023 environmental-consultant solicitation or the 2026 subdivision MOU

OCII staff presentation prepared for the August 13, 2026 Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee meeting on the proposed Block 12 West MOU and affordable-housing RFP; it states 'No entitlements remain under Mission Bay Plan Documents' and lays out the preliminary subdivision (no record of the meeting itself, such as minutes or an agenda, was found)

OCII presents a proposed personal services contract with ICF Consulting (already the selected firm) for environmental review to study increasing the bulk, density and height limits on Blocks 4 East and 12 West, in a June 8, 2023 presentation for the OCII Commission's June 20, 2023 meeting, establishing that planning work on this parcel predates the 2026 MOU by several years

The August 13, 2026 CAC presentation's own 'next steps' slide targets OCII Commission approval of the MOU for September 2026, alongside a related informational RFP item for affordable-housing development including childcare space; as of this record's last verification, no such vote had appeared on a published Commission agenda (it was absent from the Sep 1, 2026 agenda; no later agenda or notice was read)

DBI demolition permit 201712055462, to 'demolish 1 story storage bldg' at 385 Channel, is recorded as complete (filed Dec 5, 2017; approved Feb 16, 2018; issued Feb 22, 2018), clearing the one-story warehouse structure from the parcel
Demolition permit 201712055462 issued for the one-story warehouse structure on the parcel (the permit's issue date; the start of demolition work is not dated in the permit record)

costs.what: Demolition of a one-story storage building at 385 Channel under DBI permit 201712055462 (estimated and revised cost both $179,000)

facts.value: 385 Channel St (Mission Bay South Block 12 West; APN 8710-006)
~1.16 acres, ~265 units, up to 90 ft height (preliminary, subject to change)
~0.43 acres, ~270 units with an inclusionary affordable requirement, up to 250 ft height (preliminary, subject to change)

Undeveloped as of December 2015 (2015 Long-Range Property Management Plan lists Block 12 West as 'Vacant Lot/Land'); a one-story storage building on the parcel was demolished under a permit recorded complete 2019-05-17. Whether it is currently used for parking is not stated in any source read.

FOCIL-MB LLC (controlled by Farallon Capital Management, successor-in-interest to original Mission Bay master developer Catellus Development Corp), obligated under Owner Participation Agreements to contribute parcels to OCII for affordable housing
Not yet selected -- no developer named for either half of the split parcel as of this record's last verification; OCII's CAC presentation references a forthcoming RFP for the affordable-housing half
Address 385 Channel created for Mission Bay block 8710, lot 006 via over-the-counter alterations permit M401947, issued June 17, 2013

open_questions: Has the OCII Commission voted on the MOU? Not shown by any source read: it was absent from the September 1, 2026 agenda (which announces the next regular meeting for September 15, 2026). No agenda, minutes or cancellation notice for September 15 was read; re-check before relying on this.
No named developer was found for either half of the split parcel; OCII's presentation references a forthcoming RFP for the affordable-housing half only.

No firm entitlement timeline beyond 'environmental review, late 2026' was found; subsequent steps (Owner Participation Agreement amendment, Redevelopment Plan amendment, Design for Development, Blocks 11-12 Major Phase application, subdivision map) are listed only as an ordered sequence with no dates.

No press coverage (SF Chronicle, SF Standard, Mission Local, Potrero View, YIMBY) of the 2026 MOU proposal was found; all substantive detail traces back to OCII's own documents, so this remains a thin, single-source record pending independent coverage.
No cost, budget or subsidy figures for Block 12 West were found in any source reviewed.

No construction-start or completion date has been found for either half of the subdivided parcel, and no expected-completion milestone has been added (2026-09-20 pass): the only whole-plan-area date in OCII's own documents is the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Plan's own 30-year administrative term (Ordinance No. 335-98, effective from Nov 2, 1998), which sets when OCII's authority under the Plan ends, not when a project actually gets built -- using it as a stand-in for a construction-buildout target would misrepresent an undeveloped, still-unentitled parcel as complete in about two years. Left on the 2038+ cap until a real entitlement/construction schedule exists.

2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the site's current use is not stated in any source read (the OCII deck does not describe it; the 2015 plan says 'Vacant Lot/Land'); the earlier 'surface parking lot' wording had no source and was removed. The OCII CAC agenda URL previously cited returns 404; no record of the August 13, 2026 meeting itself was found.
